description:
## The smell

causal.rs reconstructs, by replaying an ordered stream, decisions the compiler makes at a specific instant and does not record.

## What is and is not already emitted

The causal ATOMS are on the stream. work_graph.applied serializes the whole AppliedStep -- changed, movements, blocked, and wakes, each wake {cause, job, disposition} (jsonl.rs write_wake). No field is dropped.

What is missing is the LINK. A wake says 'job J is woken by cause C'. J's own later completion says what J read and changed, but not why it ran. Nothing ties the evaluation to the cause, so a consumer re-pairs them by scanning positions. That is the interval rule: for evaluation e of F at t, moved inputs are (F's reads UNION F's blocked-set from its previous completion) with a movement in [F's previous conclusion, t).

The same hole exists on the product side: PRODUCT_EVALUATED carries (key, request, outcome) and no cause, so Replay::evaluate_product rebuilds triggers by the same interval scan.

## Where 'derived, never stored' came from

causal.rs, Wake{cause} and write_wake all landed in ONE commit, db83fb0c2 (fz-kdt.34, PR #106). This is not an old design that newer tools overtook: the replay and the emission capability arrived together.

The rationale is the arc PR's own scope note -- give the trace enough causality to answer what ran and why, 'without touching what emit sites pass or costing a telemetry-off run anything'. The children repeat it as a badge (34.3 'emit sites byte-identical', 34.6 'Zero production emit-site changes'). It then reached .agent/docs/telemetry.md as the standing principle 'Causality is DERIVED, never stored', where it reads as architecture rather than as the scope note it was.

Two things undercut it:

1. The arc already crossed its own line. fz-kdt.34.3 changed the engine -- AppliedStep gained wakes -- justified as 'Strictly less discarded: the scheduler already held every one of those values at the wake site and threw them away.' That sentence applies verbatim to the evaluation->cause link, the one step it did not take.
2. The surviving half of the constraint, costing a telemetry-off run nothing, is satisfied by emitting behind the existing gate. pull.rs already does exactly this: causal_product_events_enabled / emit_causal_products emit richer causal events only when telemetry wants them. Extending that is the established mechanism.

## Measured scope -- NOT 669 lines

impl Replay is 669 lines and most of it stays. Measured by method:

Inference, in scope for deletion (~215 lines of bodies plus interval shadow types):
  cause 18, woken_by_settled 18, record_movements 32, record_wakes 19 (formula side)
  evaluate_product ~113, record_product_movement 13 (product side)
  plus Movement / WaitIdentity / WaitLookup / ProductMovement / FormulaHistory and the
  per-formula position bookkeeping inside apply

Tallying over already-emitted events, stays (restructured): settle_product 48,
record_recursive_group 42, record_publication 26, request_product 20, finish_session 20,
cache_hit 14, product 9, note_definitions 37, record_ground_shifts 37,
record_non_formula_step 15, plus new/run/take_report/assert_complete/dependency_set 57.

Also unaffected: JSONL parsing (71), CanonTables and canonical packaging (213 -- raw ids do not survive across processes, so report-time translation is real work), and the record/report surface (~550, less what fz-foq.6 folds).

Honest estimate: roughly 275-300 lines of inference deleted, not 669 and not 750.

## Why it is worth doing

- The engine does not need the interval. At enqueue_step it holds (job, cause, disposition) as a first-class Wake: it re-ran F BECAUSE of C.
- The two 'load-bearing boundaries' the module doc names are inference rules about scheduler semantics living OUTSIDE the scheduler. Wait semantics have changed before (AND-semantics fz-go4.18.41, edge-triggered waits fz-kdt.46). A measuring instrument that rots silently when the thing it measures changes is worse than none.
- uncaused_evaluations, the quantity fz-kdt.34 exists to detect, becomes a direct read.

## Proof strategy

The existing Replay is the oracle: emit, assert the emitted answer equals the replayed answer on the target fixtures, then delete.

A slice of that proof ALREADY SHIPS GREEN. causal.rs cross-checks its derived Readiness against actual Settled-use wakes (woken_by_settled), and readiness_without_settled_wake.is_empty() is asserted in three places including tests/fz2_cli.rs and the cross-fixture sweep. It is non-vacuous: readiness_caused: 6 is pinned in a fixture and a sibling assertion demands executable_fact_readiness > 0 so the class cannot go empty. So for the readiness class the emitted evidence and the derivation are already proven to agree.

## What causal.rs is, and where it goes

Measured: exactly three files name CausalReport -- public_trace_test.rs, tests/fz2_cli.rs, and pull.rs inside its #[cfg(test)] mod tests. No binary, no production path. The module is the assertion vocabulary of the compiler own test suite, published out of lib.rs:29 but shipped against by nothing.

So this arc is not about making a compiler subsystem smaller: none of it is compiler code. It is about deleting a second model of scheduler semantics that can silently lie about the north-star metric, and folding two vocabularies into one.

fz-foq.3 then moves what remains to a dev-dependency crate. Sequence matters: shrink first, move second.

comments.text:
## Prior-art constraint this ticket must answer to (fz-kdt.34.6, commit 1c7201b9b)

The replay design is deliberate, not accidental. Its stated rationale:

- 'the scheduler stores WHICH facts a job read but never at what revision, so did this formula input move since its own prior conclusion was not answerable without adding THE SECOND DEPENDENCY LEDGER fz-kdt.34 FORBIDS.' The replay exists to keep causality bookkeeping out of the compiler.
- 'This lives entirely in the sink (CanonStream, jsonl.rs). No production emit site changed, drive.rs is byte-identical, telemetry-off renders nothing.' Zero observer effect on the system being measured.
- causal is re-exported 'because integration tests and a future trace-diff read the ARTIFACT, not the compiler' -- two logs from two processes compare, and an unplanned CI log stays analysable later.
- 'Reads a public JSONL log -- nothing else' is a forcing function proving the trace is sufficient. An in-process report could reach internal state and let the trace silently rot.

## What this rules OUT

Computing the CausalReport in-process behind a flag. It reinstates the forbidden ledger, puts analysis on the measured path, and gives up post-hoc and cross-process analysis. Do not propose it.

## What this ticket actually proposes, and its honest cost

Emit the LINK, not the report: an evaluation names the wake(s) that scheduled it. All four rationales above survive -- sink-side, log stays the artifact, trace stays self-sufficient, offline analysis unchanged -- while the interval inference disappears, because a wake that names its cause answers 'did this evaluation have new evidence?' directly.

Cost I under-stated in the description: the agenda must carry 'why is this job pending' per pending job until it runs. Transient and bounded by agenda size, cleared on run -- not a historical revision ledger -- but it IS state the compiler does not keep today. That is a real, smaller tension with fz-kdt.34's constraint and the ticket must argue it explicitly rather than assume it is free.

## Countervailing evidence for acting

Same commit: 'Both boundaries are load-bearing and both were measured red first.' The inference rule was wrong twice before it was right, and it models scheduler semantics from outside the scheduler. Wait semantics have changed twice since (AND-semantics fz-go4.18.41, edge-triggered waits fz-kdt.46). fz-kdt.34's rationale explains why bookkeeping should not live in the compiler; it does not address the external model drifting from what it models.

## Archaeology: where 'derived, never stored' came from

Everything -- causal.rs, Wake{cause}, and write_wake -- landed in ONE commit, db83fb0c2 (fz-kdt.34, PR #106). So this is not an old design that newer tools overtook. The replay and the emission capability arrived together.

The actual rationale is in the arc PR's opening line. The goal was to give the trace enough identity and causality to answer 'what work ran, and why' -- **'without touching what emit sites pass or costing a telemetry-off run anything.'** The children repeat it: 34.3 'nothing new stored; emit sites byte-identical', 34.6 'Zero production emit-site changes; drive.rs byte-identical'.

So derivation-over-emission was a SCOPING CONSTRAINT of that arc, not a discovered property of the problem. It then got written into .agent/docs/telemetry.md as the standing principle 'Causality is DERIVED, never stored', where it now reads as architecture.

Two things undercut it:

1. The arc already crossed its own line. fz-kdt.34.3 changed the engine -- AppliedStep gained wakes: Vec<Wake> -- with the justification 'Strictly less discarded: the scheduler already held every one of those values at the wake site and threw them away.' The same sentence applies verbatim to the evaluation->wake link, which is the one step it did not take.

2. The remaining constraint, 'costing a telemetry-off run anything', is satisfied by emitting behind --log-telemetry. The flag honours the original constraint exactly; it does not trade it away.

Also on record from 34.6: the derivation's difficulty was known and measured, not discovered later -- 'The reads-only variant false-flags 37/30/19 fully-caused evaluations (wait-satisfied jobs) -- and that red half ships as a permanent test, so nobody simplifies the rule back.' The response to a subtle rule was to lock it with a test rather than to remove the need for the rule.

Worth keeping in view: the replay earned its keep immediately. The first hunt with it filed fz-kdt.13, .56, .57, .58 and .59. This ticket is about its shape now that it has paid for itself, not about whether it should have been built.

title: An evaluation should name the wake that scheduled it
